ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: There are 27 little cubes, so using all of them to build one larger cube means the larger cube must be 3 by 3 by 3. In a 3 by 3 by 3 cube, the small-cube positions are: 8 corner positions, each exposing 3 mutually adjacent faces; 12 edge positions, each exposing 2 adjacent faces; 6 face-center positions, each exposing 1 face; and 1 interior position, exposing no faces. Each little cube has exactly 3 mutually adjacent red faces. Therefore, at every corner position, orient the cube so the 3 exposed faces are the 3 red faces. At every edge position, orient the cube so the 2 exposed faces are two of its red faces. At every face-center position, orient the cube so the 1 exposed face is red. The interior cube does not matter because none of its faces are exposed. Thus every exposed unit square on the surface of the large cube can be red, so all 6 faces of the large cube can be completely red. Since a cube has only 6 faces total, the maximum is 6.
